To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fetal erythroblastic cells are not the optimal target cell for non-invasive fetal diagnosis and that the use of a cell type-independent method is recommended for the enrichment of fetal cells in maternal blood.

(a) Fetal cells present in the maternal blood of pregnant women are not restricted to erythroblasts and (b) the use of reverse FISH with semi-automated microscopy for the detection of fetal cells in maternal blood is a promising approach to non-invasive prenatal genetic diagnosis.

1) fetal erythroblastic cells are not the optimal target cells for non-invasive diagnosis, and 2) the use of reverse FISH and automated scanning microscopy for the detection of fetal cells in maternal blood is feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of noninvasive prenatal genetic diagnosis using fetal cells present in the maternal circulation.
the development of a non-invasive prenatal diagnostic technique based on the identification of fetal cells in maternal blood.
the search for a reliable and efficient non-invasive prenatal test for the detection of fetal cells in maternal blood.
